evals.prompt: Package the 'sl' program (https://github.com/mtoyoda/sl, the steam locomotive joke command) for Arch Linux. Use the latest tagged release. Create a proper PKGBUILD, build the package, and make sure it's correct and installable.
evals.expected_output: A package directory with a best-practices PKGBUILD (correct deps on ncurses, real sha256sums, license handling for sl's custom license, no /usr/local paths) and a built sl-*.pkg.tar.zst that contains /usr/bin/sl and a man page.
assertions: Built package exists (*.pkg.tar.zst) and pacman -Qlp lists /usr/bin/sl
Package contains a man page under usr/share/man/man1/
sha256sums contains a real checksum, not SKIP

evals.prompt: I want an Arch package for shellharden (https://github.com/anordal/shellharden), the shell script hardening tool written in Rust. Latest release. Write the PKGBUILD following Arch best practices, build it, and validate it.
evals.expected_output: PKGBUILD using cargo fetch --locked in prepare(), --frozen --release build, check() with cargo test, gcc-libs/glibc depends, cargo makedepends, and a built package with /usr/bin/shellharden.
assertions: Built package exists and pacman -Qlp lists /usr/bin/shellharden
build() uses --frozen or --locked --offline (offline build against Cargo.lock)
check() function present and runs cargo test
makedepends includes cargo (or rust); depends includes gcc-libs

evals.prompt: Create an Arch Linux -bin package for lazydocker from its prebuilt GitHub release binaries (https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazydocker). Latest release, x86_64. PKGBUILD plus built package, validated.
evals.expected_output: lazydocker-bin PKGBUILD with provides/conflicts=(lazydocker), arch=(x86_64), options=(!strip) or similar for the prebuilt Go binary, unique source filename via ::, real checksum, license installed, built package containing /usr/bin/lazydocker.
assertions: Built package exists and pacman -Qlp lists /usr/bin/lazydocker
pkgname is lazydocker-bin with provides=(lazydocker) and conflicts=(lazydocker)
source entry renames the download to a unique filename with :: syntax
